contracts.existing_state: Start requires the existing historical SQLite schema; startup must not create it or alter retained rows/schema.
contracts.negative_verification: Unauthenticated verify, management and MCP requests return 401 without X-Mrj-User. Caller identity headers never grant authority.
contracts.browser_login: GET auth/connexion creates a durable single-use host/client-bound transaction, a host-only HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Lax binding cookie and S256 authorization request.
contracts.pkce_and_cookie_binding: Callback uses the server-owned PKCE verifier; wrong browser binding or host never yields a session. Concurrent tabs retain distinct binding cookies.
contracts.jwt_profile: Only ES256 signed by the trusted TLS JWKS, correct issuer/audience/azp/nonce, valid time bounds and optional matching at_hash can establish identity. Injected JWK/JKU and ambiguous JSON are rejected.
contracts.transaction_consumption: A correct callback consumes its transaction before any upstream token request. Neither retry after upstream failure nor concurrent replay can duplicate a session.
contracts.business_mapping: Each access resolves issuer and immutable subject through vision_gestion.identifier; inactive/unknown or changed principals cannot retain authority. Email claims are never an account mapping.
contracts.session_isolation: A browser session is bound to its host. Browser responses contain neither upstream access/refresh/id tokens nor nonce.
contracts.csrf: Unsafe original methods require exact same-origin and the session CSRF token, including consent/logout/revoke-other operations.
contracts.management: Management requires a business administrator, operator-qualified MFA policy, and signed auth_time newer than qualified_after and less than 900 seconds old. An amr claim alone cannot establish MFA.
contracts.refresh_outage: Provider errors/truncated responses preserve the browser session and yield recoverable unavailability. Definitive invalid_grant on refresh removes the local session; a mismatched refreshed subject is refused.
contracts.logout: Logout removes the local session even when provider revocation fails. Unrelated sessions remain usable.
contracts.mcp_metadata: Vision and Audition publish distinct resource URLs, scopes and authorization-server metadata.
contracts.mcp_registration: Only bounded exact HTTPS redirect registrations and auth method none are accepted; registration must never fetch a caller URL.
contracts.mcp_consent: A request is bound to its browser session, exact registered redirect, audience, state and S256 challenge. Another session cannot read or consume it. Refusal emits access_denied without a code.
contracts.mcp_token_binding: Authorization code is single-use, requires matching client/redirect/PKCE, and cannot be used across resource audiences. Access tokens require an unrevoked live parent browser session.
contracts.mcp_refresh_replay: A refresh rotates tokens. Reusing a consumed refresh commits revocation of the entire family, including the newly issued access/refresh pair.
contracts.tls_and_redirects: Native transport uses loopback TLS with SNI log.mrj.am and trusted CA; wrong certificates and HTTP redirects are not accepted.
contracts.bounded_parsing: Duplicated credential/host headers, duplicate form/JSON members, overlarge bodies and unsafe redirect targets cannot produce a successful identity.
contracts.diagnostics: Neither stdout/stderr nor HTTP error responses disclose provider tokens, client secrets, browser bindings or fixture identity documents. Verification success may disclose only its contractually required username.

limits: A synthetic TLS OIDC server is not the actual Kanidm implementation or production SSO.
SQL and SQLite fixtures are invented; no production state is copied.
Separate real-Kanidm qualification, host isolation, resource/traffic and full cutover tests remain necessary.
This local independent test author does not create protected forge policy or deployment approval.
